title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 sketchbook spatial refinement — pass 2
scope: Backend-only refinement following page-level review of Rakow BIB 87384. This pass narrows Maricopa, Hesperia and Port Antonio using contemporary transport evidence, historical-site controls and harbour geometry, and records one additional nonblank working-note page.
frontend_policy: No public Pages changes. Do not expose sketchbook images, thumbnails, derived polygons or viewpoint hypotheses on the public map without a later explicit decision.
method_guard: A dated place inscription secures place/date but does not automatically prove a collecting excursion or exact viewpoint.
Rail timetables can constrain observation context without proving that a sketch was drawn aboard a particular train.
Later photographs and modern coordinates are controls for persistent geometry only; they are not substitutes for 1892 evidence.
When a landmark match is plausible but not unique, preserve a view sector rather than a point.

secure_sketchbook_evidence: Cactus-Wüste bei Maricopa (Arizona) / 24. April 1892 [high-probability visual reading]

correspondence_context.statement: On 22 April Rudolf wrote from Tempe that the party would finish there the next day, go to Maricopa to spend the night, and take the Sunday-morning train toward California.
correspondence_context.chronology_inference: 22 April 1892 was Friday; the stated plan implies Tempe→Maricopa on Saturday 23 April, overnight at Maricopa, and westward departure Sunday 24 April. The dated Maricopa cards independently confirm presence there on 24 April.

historical_site_control.result: The 1892 stop is compatible with the present Maricopa railroad-town location rather than the older Maricopa Wells/Maricopaville sites.

basis.source: City of Maricopa local history / General Plan
basis.finding: Maricopa became the junction of Southern Pacific and Maricopa & Phoenix railroads in July 1887 at the final/current town site.
Current site established by railroad in 1887.

basis.title: Maricopa Railroad Map, 1915
basis.finding: Large-scale 1:1,200 station map of railroad lands, tracks and structures; useful later georeferencing control for the junction footprint.

basis.title: Arizona, Maricopa. Southern Pacific Railroad station
basis.finding: Photographic control of the Maricopa depot and baggage/passenger environment; no known restrictions on publication, though retained only as backend reference here.

contemporary_timetable_control.finding: Published railroad table states Southern Pacific westbound passes Maricopa at approximately 6:35 a.m.; the same time appears in later 1892 issues.

transport_context.guard: The May timetable is very close in date and repeated later in 1892, but an April 24 issue-specific timetable has not yet been recovered. Treat 6:35 a.m. as strong contextual control, not exact proof of Rudolf's train time.

interpretive_revision.reason: The correspondence explicitly frames Maricopa as an overnight rail transfer before the California train. No source currently documents a separate collecting excursion at Maricopa on 24 April.

terrain_hypothesis.reason: The continuous rugged range and broad desert foreground remain morphologically compatible with Sierra Estrella northwest of the junction; Table Top remains an alternative. Transport-context refinement does not itself identify the mountain.
terrain_hypothesis.recommended_next_test: Generate DEM horizon profiles from a set of points along the 1887/1915 junction and first westbound rail miles; compare peak order, relative angular widths and skyline notches against pages 5 and 9.

hesperia.identification: Hesperia, 5 May 1892 — strong correspondence/ecology match; no secure place/date inscription on the sketch
hesperia.correspondence_anchor: Agua Caliente letter, 7 May 1892, retrospectively describing Hesperia on 5 May
correspondence_details: found rooms at a hotel near the station
at daybreak saw a vast desert plain surrounded by mountains with a snow-topped San Bernardino summit
tree-like Yucca brevifolia rose from the desert 'like a forest'
the party then took a pretty far morning excursion into the desert before leaving by afternoon train

historic_station_hotel_proxy.status: precise modern marker proxy, not the exact building centroid
historic_station_hotel_proxy.station_evidence: Hesperia Train Station marker states the 1887–1952 15 × 20 ft wooden station stood directly across Hesperia Road from the marker; marker is on Spruce Street just west of Hesperia Road.
historic_station_hotel_proxy.hotel_relation: The Hesperia Hotel marker is on the same monument/area, independently matching Rudolf's statement that his hotel was near the station.

historical_maps.title: Map No. 1 of Hesperia San Bernardino County, Cal.; showing town and acre properties
Hesperia
historical_maps.date: circa 1890; catalogue notes Hesperia laid out in 1891

result.secure_infrastructure_area: Spruce Street / Hesperia Road historic depot-hotel cluster
result.mountain_view_sector: roughly 129°–134° from the station proxy toward the San Bernardino high country
result.reason_exact_viewpoint_stays_low: Rudolf explicitly distinguishes the daybreak view at the hotel/station from a later 'pretty far excursion into the desert'. The drawing contains no railway/hotel architecture and may derive from that excursion.

hesperia.recommended_geometry: Historic depot-hotel point as itinerary/infrastructure anchor plus a separate broader morning-excursion field area; do not collapse page 17 to the station coordinate.

port_antonio.identification: Probable Port Antonio harbour view, late February 1892
port_antonio.archive_anchor: BLA-D00736 · 017:90: Rudolf records landing at Port Antonio on 28 February and later mentions his impressions of Port Antonio during the Bowden passage.
port_antonio.visible_configuration: Banded lighthouse on a low foreground point at left; a channel opens behind it; a palm-covered island/shore lies at right; mountains form the rear horizon.

folly_point_control.morphology: round masonry/brick tower with red/orange-red and white horizontal bands
folly_point_control.assessment: The date and conspicuous horizontal banding make Folly Point a strong lighthouse candidate.

navy_island_control.assessment: Navy Island is a plausible palm-covered right-hand landmass, but the sketch is too schematic for a unique island identification.

harbour_geometry_control.source: Admiralty Chart No. 453, Port Antonio, surveyed 1790 / published 1815
harbour_geometry_control.use: Persistent harbour topology: Navy Island, East/West harbour basins, headlands and approach channel; lighthouse postdates chart.

later_shipboard_control.finding: A photograph from the refrigerated fruit carrier Jamaica Planter was taken at sea looking west by south toward Folly Point Lighthouse, with Navy Island in the background.
later_shipboard_control.use_guard: This is not evidence for Rudolf's 1892 ship position. It demonstrates that a shipboard view can naturally align Folly Point and Navy Island in the same visual field.

view_sector_revision.previous_model: offshore north of Port Antonio facing generally south
view_sector_revision.refined_model: broad offshore northern-to-northeastern approach/departure sector; exact azimuth unresolved
view_sector_revision.reason: The lighthouse/island topology works from northern offshore approaches, while the later RMG shipboard control shows that positions east/northeast of Folly also produce lighthouse + Navy Island alignments. The sketch's left/right placement alone cannot uniquely recover vessel position because perspective, cropping and the identity of the right-hand landmass remain uncertain.

port_antonio.recommended_geometry: A broad offshore harbour-approach/departure sector, not a point. Keep the Folly Point identification stronger than the Navy Island identification.

additional_page_review.blank_page_policy: Visually blank filmed leaves were ignored.

page_28.observation: Three short handwritten lines, apparently numerical/geographical working notes, are visible after rotation/contrast enhancement.
page_28.guard: Do not OCR-force a reading. Preserve page 28 as an unresolved calculation/note until palaeographic reading is secure.
page_28.relation_to_page_27: Possibly related to the adjacent New York–Bremen distance calculation, but this is only a sequencing hypothesis.

key_revisions_from_previous_pass: Maricopa pages should be interpreted primarily as transit/overnight landscape observations rather than evidence for a separate Maricopa collecting excursion.
The current Maricopa railroad-town location is historically valid for 1892 because the final junction site was established in 1887.
Hesperia infrastructure can now be localized to the Spruce Street / Hesperia Road depot-hotel cluster, while the sketch viewpoint remains a broader excursion-area problem.
Folly Point is now a very strong p23 lighthouse candidate; Port Antonio overall rises to high-probability, but exact vessel position and Navy Island identification remain below secure level.
Page 28 is nonblank and should remain as an unresolved working-note record.
next_tests: Maricopa: georeference the 1915 station map and compute DEM skylines along the junction and first westbound Southern Pacific miles; compare against pages 5 and 9.
Hesperia: recover the downloadable Huntington townsite-map image, register it against the station marker/rail alignment, then model plausible morning excursion radii constrained by train times.

Port Antonio: digitize Folly Point/Navy Island/headland outlines from the Admiralty chart and test p23 against candidate viewing bearings; keep the result as a sector unless a unique topology emerges.
Page 28: attempt human palaeographic comparison with page 27 numerals/letterforms before any OCR.
